newsitem.title: UK: EURO OIL SWAPS MOSTLY UP BUT GAS OIL, JET LOWER.
newsitem.headline: EURO OIL SWAPS MOSTLY UP BUT GAS OIL, JET LOWER.

text.p: European oil swaps were $1- $4 firmer on Wednesday on fuel oil, gasoline and naphtha front months despite lower crude futures, but gas oil and jet differentials slipped.
Brent crude CFDs were quiet and well offered. Next week and the following three weeks were offered around October -23/22 cents.
Brent Sept/Oct was -12/-10 cents with Oct/Nov -14/-10 cents. The Brent Sept/Oct traded three times, twice at -11 cents and once at -10 cents.
Gas oil cracks were broadly unchanged, but differentials for EN590, 0.2 diesel and jet were talked lower.

A jet deal was confirmed at $24.50 for the fourth quarter, $0.25 below Tuesday's deal level, with indications of a similar decline in October and November as 1998 quarters. Spreads were seen unchanged.
A banker said that airlines had begun to hedge on the second quarter/third quarter 1998 spread, having largely completed trading activities over first/second quarter.

At $2.50-$2.75 for the fourth quarter, 0.2 was seen around $0.50 lower than early in the week, while EN590 was seen $0.75-$1 lower on the week at around $8.50 for fourth quarter. This left the EN590/0.2 spread as much $0.50 down at $5.75-$6.00, dealers said.
High sulphur fuel oil swaps were up to $1 a tonne firmer despite easier screen crude. Traders said August was pegged around $94.50 with September between $95-95.50.
"There is very good bunker demand and prompt supplies are tight," said one.
Wet barges traded around $96.00 fob ARA.
Gasoline August swap quotes meanwhile jumped $3-$4 to $213-$215 on the back of a firming prompt barge market that saw trades as high as $220 FOB AR.
September swaps were meanwhile seen $1-$1.50 higher at $197-$197.50.

A late Tuesday naphtha physical deal at $197 underlined bullish prompt indications and helped to lift August swaps by $0.50 to $193-$194 despite lower crude futures. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 8185
